home.subtitle: Settlement is decided solely by the first signed Chainlink OCR2 report after expiry — no intermediary decides the outcome. A market can be opened with just over 1 USDT.
home.why1: Open a market with just over 1 USDT. No one's approval needed.
home.why2: Settlement is decided by the first signed Chainlink report after expiry — verified on-chain, final in seconds. No voting, no dispute bond, no appeal window.
home.why3: Exposure is released gradually as expiry approaches and can be claimed at any time. Trading fees accrue in real time to the makers present at each trade as pending inventory, claimable in the LP desk.
home.settleCensusValue: 172,714 reports · 24 round jumps · Snapshot fallback at expiry
home.settleRuleTag: Permissionless · Anyone can submit · Includes scripts/settle.js
home.settleNode1Sub: Pairs the last pre-expiry & first post-expiry OCR2 reports via on-chain secp256k1 verification — one outcome, zero disputes.
home.settleNode2Sub: Signed reports can be recovered from failed transmissions. If rounds jump across expiry, a matching on-chain snapshot can certify the pair.
home.settleNode3Sub: The on-chain post-expiry delay limit is fixed at 10s; if exceeded or unsettled after 48h, the market voids at 0.5 USDT instead of using stale prints.
home.how1: Pick a market. Buy YES or NO.
home.how2: Wait for expiry. Prices move as people trade.
home.how3: The first post-expiry report decides which side redeems — 1 USDT per token.

help.title: Veritas: a fast, permissionless prediction market
help.sub: Short-duration markets on crypto prices. Anyone can open one, anyone can trade. Settlement is decided jointly by the last signed report before expiry and the first one after it, with the ruling price taken from the first report after expiry — no intermediary decides the outcome.
help.v1Title: Open a market with just over 1 USDT
help.v1: No listing review, no gatekeeper. Seed a market with a little over 1 USDT of collateral and it is live.
help.v2: Which side redeems is decided by the first signed Chainlink OCR2 report after expiry — verified directly on-chain, not by a person you have to trust.
help.v3: Swaps pay a dynamic fee per leg: 0.50% when the market opens, rising toward 3.00% as expiry approaches. The climb is anchored on the 15-minute market — shorter markets climb faster, longer markets slower. Zero protocol take — 100% accrues in real time to active makers as pending inventory, claimable in each market's LP desk.
help.risk: Making markets is not free money. When the price moves, better-informed traders trade against you exactly when your quote lags the real price — that adverse-selection loss (LVR) is the real cost of providing liquidity, and fees only partly offset it. Veritas shrinks the risk rather than erasing it: a maker's exposure winds down automatically as expiry approaches. Additionally, the post-expiry delay tolerance is an on-chain protocol constant fixed at 10s (changing it requires a program upgrade): if exceeded, or if nobody settles within 48 hours of expiry, the market is voided and every token redeems at 0.5 USDT instead of settling on stale pricing.
help.d1: Display prices and settlement verification use two separate paths: live spot prices shown on this site are read from each feed's on-chain Chainlink Store Transmissions account (the small age next to each price is that print's own age), whereas market settlement does NOT read that Store account — settlement evidence comes from the signed OCR2 reports carried inside oracle transmit transactions, verified directly on-chain.
help.d2: Settlement verifies two signed Chainlink OCR2 reports straddling expiry: the pre-expiry report and the first post-expiry report, checked on-chain against the feed's oracle roster, config digest, and round adjacency (or an expiry snapshot).
help.d3: Charts use Coinbase candles for reference only. They are never used for settlement.
help.d4: This deployment runs on Solana devnet. On devnet, Chainlink prints may pause or skip rounds occasionally — the age label next to every price shows exact print freshness.
help.deepWhyLabel: Why we built it this way
help.a0Title: 01 · Low threshold: Built for high-frequency fast markets
help.a0: The 15-minute and 24-hour markets (plus a 2-minute sandbox demo lane) run side by side with staggered openings, so new markets open while others settle. Short-horizon price swings move fast, and traders want to spin up a market the moment they spot a setup; if opening a 15-minute market required heavy market-making capital or a listing committee, fast markets would never get off the ground. A market that resolves in minutes should not demand heavy upfront capital from its creator.
help.a0Sub: We lowered market creation to just over 1 USDT (1,000,001 micro-units) with zero manual approval. On creation, the contract calibrates initial depth from the seed deposit and duration T via L₀ = budget / (φ(0)·√T) at 50:50, binds a whitelisted Chainlink OCR2 state account, and initializes the MarketSnapshot PDA. Under the hood, every 1 USDT mints 1 YES + 1 NO (mergeable 1:1 back to 1 USDT via merge_token at any time while open), making fast-market creation effortless while guaranteeing 100% collateralization by construction.
help.a0Fee: A threshold this low is only practical on Solana. Creating a market, seeding it and settling it together cost a fraction of a cent in transaction fees, so a pool of this size remains economical. At EVM gas prices, the transaction fees for the same operations would consume a substantial share of a 1 USDT pool.
help.a1Title: 03 · Liquidity that stays to settlement: pm-AMM (L_eff = L₀√(T−t))
help.a1: As a fast market approaches expiry, the outcome becomes clearer. If a traditional constant-product pool (x·y=k) locks liquidity statically in the pool, LPs get bled dry by arbitrageurs (LVR adverse selection) in the final minutes — forcing makers to pull liquidity early right when traders need depth the most.
help.a1Sub: We implement Paradigm's pm-AMM Gaussian invariant (P = Φ((y − x) / L_eff)), decaying effective liquidity L_eff = L₀·√(T − t) smoothly with the square root of time remaining. Before every trade, LP action, or settlement, compute_accrual scales active reserves to the new L_eff at constant price P and credits the released YES/NO inventory pro-rata to LPs (withdrawable and mergeable back to USDT at any time) — winding down maker risk automatically while keeping calibrated depth right up to expiry.
help.a2Title: 02 · No dispute window: Second-level finality & 3-tier settlement defense
help.a2: In a 15-minute fast market, waiting hours for a committee vote or dispute window breaks the product. Delivering no dispute window so anyone can permissionlessly settle via UI or CLI script requires one guarantee: the contract itself must verify on-chain that a print is the first valid price after expiry, without jamming on network hiccups.
help.a2Sub: Across six Chainlink OCR2 feeds on Devnet, 172,714 reports landed during the full UTC day of November 22, 2026. The round sequence jumped 24 times. When a jump straddles expiry, a matching on-chain snapshot can certify the two reports for settlement. The census lists every transaction signature.
help.censusEvidence: View census data and transaction signatures
help.a2Tier1: Tier 1 (Normal path · Straddling adjacent-round squeeze): Anyone can permissionlessly submit the two signed OCR2 reports straddling expiry T (pre < T ≤ post). The contract verifies secp256k1 oracle multi-signatures and round adjacency on-chain (round + 1, or round 6 rolling into round 1 of the next epoch), locking in the first post-expiry price and preventing cherry-picking.
help.a2Tier2: Tier 2 (Failed transmissions and snapshot fallback): Anyone can extract a signed OCR2 report from a failed transmission and submit it for on-chain verification. If the two reports straddling expiry have nonadjacent rounds, the contract can verify the pair against matching snapshots recorded via take_snapshot within 10 seconds of expiry.
help.a2Tier3: Tier 3 (Ultimate backstop · On-chain 0.5 refund): When an unrecorded oracle round skip coincides with a missing snapshot, or the first report exceeds the 10-second post-expiry tolerance / 48h resolve window, the fallback triggers — the contract rejects stale pricing and voids the market so both YES and NO redeem at 0.5 USDT.
help.a2Fallback: Even if the protocol team did nothing at all, anyone can still settle any expired market within the 48-hour window — either by clicking "Settle now" directly on the market page (where your browser extracts the OCR2 signatures straight from the RPC with zero backend dependency) or by running the open-source settlement script to invoke resolve_market:
help.a2FallbackNote: Prerequisites: run from the repository root with Node.js installed and npm install completed at the root; provide a local keypair with a small amount of Devnet SOL for fees (reads ANCHOR_WALLET, WALLET_PATH, or defaults to ~/.config/solana/id.json); RPC URL is read from SOLANA_RPC or RPC_URL (defaults to Devnet). Pass only the market pubkey — the script automatically locates both straddling OCR2 reports and submits resolve_market permissionlessly.
help.footnote: Veritas currently runs on Solana Devnet — a demo environment, and no real funds are involved.
help.quickTitle: New here? Start in three steps
help.q1Title: Open Sandbox or connect a Devnet wallet
help.q1: Click "Open Sandbox Account (Devnet)" to start immediately with a browser keypair — or connect Phantom / Solflare switched to Devnet if you want to create markets or provide LP.
help.q2Title: Auto top-up or claim test funds
help.q2: When a balance runs low, it is topped up to 0.04 SOL and 30 test USDT (enough to place orders and redeem). Connected real wallets can open "Test Funds" in the top-right header to claim 100 test USDT (once every 24h) plus official Devnet SOL.
help.q2Cooldown: Already claimed today — come back tomorrow
help.q3: Open any live market, pick YES or NO, and confirm. Track positions under Portfolio (Me), and redeem 1:1 on the same market page after settlement.
help.ex1: Target 60,000; the first report after expiry reads 60,120 — above the target, so YES redeems 1:1 and NO expires worthless.
help.ex2: Same Target Price under the fixed 10-second on-chain delay limit: if the first report lands 12 seconds late, the market voids automatically and every token redeems at 0.5 USDT.
